name: Ruincraft Corpskin Manifesto Jacket
description:
A Shelf-made oversized jacket assembled from weather-membrane scraps, transit seat vinyl, and deconstructed Ouroboros-brand workwear. Every panel is covered in hand-stenciled text — excerpts from the Meridian Labor Accord (crossed out), pirate-broadcast transcripts, and the phrase ΦUANTA IS A LIE repeated across the left shoulder in drip-paint red. Corporate logos appear inverted, stitched upside-down as deliberate mockery.

No two jackets are identical. The construction itself is the statement — visible seams, mismatched thread, patches over patches.
functionality: Weather-membrane panels provide moderate acid-rain resistance. Deep interior pockets are large enough for a compressed rebreather. Deliberately unfinished edges allow quick field modification.
what_it_says: This person rejects the system loudly, on purpose, and has the craft to make it beautiful.
story_hooks: A specific jacket contains a complete transcript of an internal Ouroboros memo about Shelf water contamination, hidden in the layered text.
CorpSec has begun cataloguing these jackets as gang-adjacent material — wearing one is now grounds for a stop-and-scan.
A Tier 5 fashion house has begun producing luxury replicas at Φ4,000 each, and the Shelf makers are furious.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately deconstructed oversized jacket that reads as organized chaos—street-worn armor for anti-corporate agitators. The silhouette is baggy and slouched, panels of different weights creating an intentionally asymmetrical drape. It commands attention through visual noise and defiant messaging rather than polish.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and deliberately ill-fitting—shoulders drop past natural shoulder line, sleeves are cropped unevenly, body hangs loose enough to layer augmentation rigs beneath. Built for movement and concealment, not aesthetics.
physical_description.primary_material: Composite scraps: weather-membrane synthetic (waterproof, translucent in places), recycled transit seat vinyl (creased and worn texture), deconstructed Ouroboros workwear cotton-blend panels. Mix of rigid and flexible materials creates visual texture breaks.
physical_description.texture: Extremely tactile and varied—smooth vinyl sections contrast with rough membrane patches, visible top-stitching in mismatched thread colors (black, red, white), hand-stenciled text that sits raised on the weave, drip-paint overlay creating slight dimensional texture on left shoulder. Deliberately weathered appearance with fraying edges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominately industrial gray and off-white base, accented with transit-seat vinyl blacks and taupes. Inverted corporate logos appear in faded original colors (muted blues, silvers). Bright red drip-paint text (ΦUANTA IS A LIE) across left shoulder is the only vivid color—intentionally jarring.
physical_description.closures: Mismatched: left side has friction-fit magnetic snaps (salvaged, slightly non-functional), right side has hand-sewn button substitutes (bolts, plastic shards), center front left open by design. Deliberately non-uniform and difficult to secure.
distinctive_features: Hand-stenciled text covering 60% of visible surface—excerpts from Meridian Labor Accord struck through with marker, pirate-broadcast snippets, repeated ΦUANTA IS A LIE
Inverted corporate logos deliberately stitched upside-down as mockery, appearing across back and sleeves
Visible seam work with contrasting thread colors—no attempt to hide construction
Layered patches: vinyl patches over membrane tears, fabric scraps sewn directly atop existing wear
Left shoulder features drip-paint overlay creating dimensional red text effect
Multiple hidden pockets with zipper pulls made from salvaged transit tokens
Right arm features a repurposed transit route map stenciled in fading ink
No two panels match in material weight or finish—intentional visual discord
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage/underground — anti-corporate messaging, hand-made construction, deliberately rejected Tier 2-3 brand aesthetics
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals radical labor solidarity, Shelf collective membership, active rejection of QUANTA corporate systems. Wearer is post-scarcity resistant, networked with pirate broadcast audiences, operating in ungoverned zones. Deliberately provocative toward corpo security.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered, heavily worn, covered in visible repairs. Looks aged even when new due to construction method. Stenciled text fades unevenly with exposure and friction. Patches develop their own patinas—this is the intended 'finish.'

image_prompt: Oversized deconstructed jacket on angular cyberpunk model with visible augmentation ports, shot against gritty concrete wall covered in faded stencil art. Moody industrial lighting casting harsh shadows across hand-stenciled text—ΦUANTA IS A LIE glowing faintly in red drip-paint across left shoulder. Visible mismatched seams, weathered vinyl panels, upside-down corporate logos stitched throughout. Model's posture is defiant, one hand gripping a torn pocket. Dark underground setting, neon reflected on weathered materials. Shallow depth of field highlighting text details. Cyberpunk aesthetic, anti-corporate street fashion --ar 2:3 --v 6
